item.title: BOK Warns of Risks From Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs: Yonhap
item.description: The Bank of Korea warned that single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. could deepen market concentration, amplify volatility and intensify one-way trading flows, according to a local report.

item.title: Fewer Ships Transiting Hormuz Along Oman Coast After U-Turns
item.description: The number of vessels sailing through the Strait of Hormuz along the Omani coast fell to a trickle on Sunday, a day after several exiting along that route made sharp reversals, underscoring Iran’s continued efforts to maintain its grip on the waterway.

item.title: Modi’s Biofuel Push Comes Under Pressure as Motorists Protest
item.description: Indian motorists will gather in New Delhi on Sunday, in the first major protest against a flagship biofuel program intended to reduce crude imports and support farm incomes.

item.title: Wang Yi Says China Welcomes Stronger European Business Relations
item.description: China welcomes deeper cooperation with Swedish and European businesses, which will benefit all parties involved, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in a meeting with Investor AB Chairman Jacob Wallenberg in Stockholm on July 4, according to a statement from the ministry on Sunday.

item.title: NZ Pledges Trade Talks With Brazil, Europe Within Five Years
item.description: New Zealand’s governing National Party will begin negotiations for seven new trade deals within five years should it win the November election, Trade Minister Todd McClay said.

item.title: Investors Looking for Shelter From AI Storm Are Turning to India
item.description: After losing out big on the global AI rally, Indian equities are regaining the attention of investors seeking to weather the latest market turbulence.

item.title: Trump Ramps Up War on Regulations With 702 Cuts in Pipeline
item.description: The Trump administration is stepping up its efforts to cut red tape across the federal government, releasing a regulatory plan that would eliminate 702 existing administrative rules.

item.title: Germany’s Second Chance for Growth Rebound Starts Now
item.description: German data in the coming week showing the cumulative impact of the Iran war will set the stage for the government’s latest bid to awaken animal spirits in Europe’s biggest economy.

item.title: Venezuela’s Official Death Toll From Quake Rises to Almost 3,000
item.description: Venezuela‘s official death toll from last week’s twin earthquakes rose to almost 3,000 on Saturday.

item.title: Brazil’s Durigan Says Credit Lines Won’t Affect Monetary Policy
item.description: Credit measures introduced by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government do not undermine monetary policy, Finance Minister Dario Durigan said in an interview with local news website G1 published on Saturday.

item.title: Putin Signs Tax Amendments Aiming to Boost Domestic Fuel Supply
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a law to stimulate gasoline supplies to the domestic market.

item.title: India’s CG Semi Starts Production With 200 Million Chips
item.description: India’s CG Power & Industrial Solutions Ltd.’s new semiconductor unit has started production with an annual capacity of 200 million chips, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Saturday, marking a fresh milestone in the country’s goal to build a domestic chip industry and gain a foothold in the global supply chain.

item.title: Insider Trading Cases End as DOJ Dud With Few Prison Sentences
item.description: Sitting at home in the south of France, beyond the reach of US law enforcement for the better part of a decade, former Moelis and Co. banker Benjamin Taylor made what seemed like a brave choice. He returned to the US to face an insider trading charge that carried as much as five years behind bars.

item.title: Oil’s Stunning Reversal Rekindles Fears of a Global Glut
item.description: Oil prices are tumbling everywhere as a peace deal between the US and Iran unleashes a wave of supply, overwhelming demand from buyers and prompting talk of a glut of crude.

item.title: Credit Agricole Increases BPM Stake, Boosting Position in Italy
item.description: The Credit Agricole SA Campus in Paris, France, on Monday, Feb. 2, 2026. The euro-area economy grew more than expected at the end of last year, demonstrating resilience to the trade turmoil unleashed by Donald Trump.

item.title: China Issues Guide for Registering International Science Groups
item.description: China issued guidance for establishing international scientific organizations in the country, setting out registration requirements for nonprofit groups focused on scientific cooperation, exchange and governance.

item.title: Third Australian State Confirms Case of Deadly H5 Avian Flu
item.description: The major Australian state of New South Wales confirmed a case of the H5 avian influenza in a wild bird, bringing the total number of cases nationwide to six just two weeks after it was first detected on the mainland.

item.title: Tankers U-Turn in Hormuz, With Some Taking Iran Route Instead
item.description: At least eight ships attempting to leave the Persian Gulf along the Omani coast turned back between Friday and Saturday, in the latest sign that reopening the Strait of Hormuz remains complicated by Iran seeking to assert its control over the key waterway. Some of the vessels continued with their transits by switching to a route closer to Iran.

item.title: Eastern US Heat Wave Starts to Retreat While Raising Storm Risk
item.description: Extreme heat that’s seared the eastern US, strained the power grid from Maine to the Carolinas and curtailed holiday celebrations is starting to break up.

item.title: ECB Is in ‘Good Position’ Given Inflation Data, Moulin Says
item.description: The European Central Bank is in a “good position” following an interest-rate hike last month and data showing inflation has eased with the slump in oil prices, Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said on Saturday.

item.title: Total CEO Sees Mideast Producers Desperate to Sell Oil Stocks
item.description: Middle East oil producers are desperate to sell crude stockpiled during the recent Persian Gulf conflict, but gasoline and diesel inventories remain constrained due to shipping worries, TotalEnergies SE Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanné said.

item.title: Modi Says India Will Keep Expanding Oil Refining Capacity
item.description: India will continue to build new crude oil refineries in order to ensure supply chain security even as Western nations shut processing units, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said.

item.title: Charting the Global Economy: US Hiring Slows, Eurozone CPI Cools
item.description: US hiring slowed sharply in June after three months of better-than-expected jobs reports, and investors scaled back bets on a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase this year.

item.title: Oil Terminal in Russia’s St. Petersburg Comes Under Attack
item.description: Kyiv’s forces attacked an oil terminal in St. Petersburg, Russia’s second largest city, with drones overnight, local officials said, while Ukraine said a gas production facility was struck by Russia.

item.title: Macron’s Budget Finale Augurs More Political Chaos in France
item.description: The final budget showdown of Emmanuel Macron’s presidency is already gearing up to be France’s highest-stakes fiscal clash of the decade so far.

item.title: China Envisions AI, Karaoke and Coffee at Cinemas
item.description: AI agents, karaoke and coffee shops may appear at Chinese cinemas under new guidelines that encourage theaters to expand beyond traditional film screenings.

item.title: Local Lenders Set to Supercharge Crypto Trading in Germany
item.description: The cryptocurrency market in Germany is expected to gain significant momentum in the coming months as millions of people will soon be able to trade virtual currencies directly through their local banks, without having to go through specialized third-party platforms.

item.title: Russia Said It Captured Key Ukraine Stronghold in Donetsk Region
item.description: Russia announced the seizure of a strategic logistics hub in the Donetsk region and claimed full control of Ukraine’s Luhansk region, days after launching its deadliest attack on Kyiv since the war began.

item.title: Micron Breaks Ground on $9 Billion Plant Expansion in Japan
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. on Saturday broke ground on the expansion of its factory in western Japan, a ¥1.5 trillion ($9.3 billion) undertaking to produce advanced memory chips.

item.title: SK Hynix Is Said to Weigh 0.5% Fee Payout in Mega ADR Offering
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. is considering paying about 0.5% of the proceeds from its US listing — one of the largest share sales ever — to banks working on the deal, according to people familiar with the matter.
